attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

cases.label: new password of 41 characters ending in a space: SQL Server truncates nvarchar(40), PostgreSQL text keeps the space
cases.reasoning: @NewPassword nvarchar(40) silently truncates a 41-character value to 40 on SQL Server, so HASHBYTES hashes 40 'n' + FullName. The conversion declares new_password text and hashes 40 'n' + ' ' + FullName, so the stored hash differs unless the conversion truncates too.

cases.label: the new password differs from the old one only in case: the new hash is of 'PW', not of 'pw'
cases.reasoning: The stored hash is SHA2_256 of the UTF-16LE bytes of 'pw' + 'amy', so the old password is correct and the update runs. The new password 'PW' differs from the old only in case; HASHBYTES hashes its bytes as given, so the stored hash must change to that of 'PW' + 'amy'. A conversion that case-folded either password, or compared new and old under a case-insensitive collation and skipped the update, would store a different value. The hand-derived case-only case tests a refused old password, not the new hash.

cases.label: two people share a full name and both have the same stored hash; only the requested PersonID changes
cases.reasoning: Persons 2 and 3 share FullName 'amy' and the stored hash of 'pw' + 'amy', so the old password is correct for both; person 1 is 'Amy' (case differs). The UPDATE must touch only PersonID = 2: person 3, whose row would also match the password test, stays unchanged on both engines.

cases.label: NULL new password with an empty full name: NULL + '' is NULL, so the hash becomes NULL (concat would hash ''); an '' preference stays ''
cases.reasoning: Person 2's FullName is '' and the stored hash is that of 'pw' + '', so the old password is correct. @NewPassword NULL makes HASHBYTES(N'SHA2_256', NULL + FullName) NULL under CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL, even though FullName is the empty string; a conversion using concat() or COALESCE(new_password, '') would store the hash of zero bytes instead. Person 1's UserPreferences '' must stay '' (not become NULL).

cases.label: PersonID = 1 (the template) is refused even with the correct password; its row is unchanged
cases.reasoning: The stored hash is that of 'pw' + 'root', so the old password is correct and only the AND PersonID <> 1 test refuses the call; a conversion without it (the planted defect 'person 1 (the template) can change password') would store a new hash for person 1. PersonIDs 1 and 3 (a gap) confirm the predicate is on the value, not row order. The adversarial gate and its planted-defect check run on the adversarial cases alone, without the hand-derived ones, so this input is kept among them even where a hand-derived case uses a similar one.

cases.label: a full name with a trailing space changes the hashed bytes
cases.reasoning: The stored hash is that of 'pw' + 'Ab ' (with the trailing space), so the old password is correct and the new hash is computed from 'new' + 'Ab '. A conversion that rtrimmed the full name (in either hash), or hashed the new password without the full name, would store a different hash; the update also re-enables the logon, which person 2 does not have before the call.
